body:
UP-Term 1.4 adds `upkg browse`: a full-screen list of every add-on in the feed. You can install, upgrade, remove and read about add-ons from that list, with no package names to type.

Only the base (up-term.lha) changes in this release. The add-ons keep their 1.3 versions.

## upkg browse

![upkg browse: the add-on list with the cursor on up-vim](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spotUP/UP-Term/f16175eca7da4e8e56f8b6a0e4f9c71b543ed2e5/docs/screenshots/upkg-browse-list.png)

Run `upkg update` first, so the list is current. Then type:

```
upkg browse
```

The header shows how many add-ons the feed has. Each row shows an add-on's name, its version and its state: installed, upgrade (a newer version is in the feed) or available.

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Up, Down | Move the cursor |
| Enter | Show the add-on's info (`upkg info`) |
| i | Install the add-on |
| u | Upgrade the add-on |
| r | Remove the add-on, after a Yes/No question (No is the default) |
| q, Escape | Quit to the Shell |

Each action runs the normal `upkg` command in the window, so you see its output. "Press Return to go back to the list." then takes you back, with the cursor on the same add-on.

![i on up-vim: the install runs in the window](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spotUP/UP-Term/f16175eca7da4e8e56f8b6a0e4f9c71b543ed2e5/docs/screenshots/upkg-browse-install.png)

![r on up-vim, then Yes: the add-on is removed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spotUP/UP-Term/f16175eca7da4e8e56f8b6a0e4f9c71b543ed2e5/docs/screenshots/upkg-browse-remove.png)

If the list program (upkg-ui) cannot start, `upkg browse` now says so: it prints "upkg browse: upkg-ui failed (exit N)." and returns 2. Before this fix it went back to the Shell without a message.

## Install

You need a 68020 or better and AmigaOS 3.0 or newer. upkg downloads over the network: it needs a TCP/IP stack (Roadshow, Miami or AmiTCP) and AmiSSL 5, and the curl option ticked in Install.

New install:

1. Download `up-term.lha` from the assets below and unpack it with lha.
2. Double-click `Install` in the UP-Term drawer. Tick the optional parts you want, curl among them. Without Installer, use the Shell route in the kit's README.txt.
3. Reboot after Install. XCON: and PTY: are mounted from then on.
4. Open an UP-Term window and run `upkg update`, then `upkg browse`.

Upgrade from 1.3: unpack the 1.4 `up-term.lha` and run its `Install`. The first page names the installed version and offers Update (the default). Update copies only the files that changed and keeps your choices and your add-ons. `upkg` is part of the base, so a new version of it always comes with up-term.lha, never as an ipk.

## Add-ons (upkg feed)

These ipk packages are in this release's feed (`Packages`, `Packages.gz`). They keep their 1.3 versions.

| Add-on | Version | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| up-claude | 1.1 | Claude Code for the Amiga (C:Claude) |
| up-pi | 1.0 | amiga-pi, the pi coding agent |
| up-nvim | 1.0 | Neovim 0.12 in UP-Term:nvim |
| up-python | 1.0 | Python 3.14 in SYS:Python3 |
| up-git | 1.0 | git 2.56.0 |
| up-perl | 1.0 | Perl 5.42.3 |
| up-vim | 1.0 | Vim 9.2.1202 |

Without the list:

```
upkg update                 fetch the feed's package list
upkg list                   the packages the feed offers
upkg list-installed         the add-ons you have
upkg info <name>            details of one add-on
upkg install <name>         install an add-on
upkg upgrade                bring the installed add-ons up to the feed
upkg remove <name>          remove an add-on
upkg --help                 all commands
```

The .lha archives of up-claude, up-pi, up-nvim and up-python are also here. Use them to install those add-ons without upkg.

## Assets

- `up-term.lha`: the base kit, version 1.4.
- `*.ipk`, `Packages`, `Packages.gz`: the add-on feed that upkg reads.
- `upkg-index.txt`: the index of the .lha archives.
- `up-claude.lha`, `up-pi.lha`, `up-nvim.lha`, `up-python.lha`: stand-alone archives.
- `up-term-src.lha`: the source of the base.

Built from spotUP/UP-Term 2ef9ec92, upterm 5f51b85. The kit's VERSIONS file lists the commit of each repository.
